previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A female patient with end-stage renal disease, antiphospholipid syndrome, and a history of recurrent hyperkalemia was admitted for dizziness and leg tingling lasting 16 hours, symptoms she recognized from prior hyperkalemic episodes. In the emergency department, her potassium was 6.9 mEq/L with a normal EKG. She received standard medical treatment including insulin, dextrose, calcium gluconate, and albuterol nebs, followed by an initial hemodialysis session. She was admitted for monitoring and remained asymptomatic overnight. Morning labs showed potassium at 5.3 mEq/L, prompting a second 2.5-hour dialysis session. She recovered well, remained stable, and was discharged home with instructions to resume her regular dialysis schedule and have her potassium monitored at her next outpatient session. Her chronic medications, including warfarin and lamotrigine, were continued without change.

Brief Hospital Course:
Mrs. ___ is ___ w/ ESRD, antiphospholipid syndrome, on 
dialysis (RUE AVF ___, does not make any urine), lupus, HTN 
who presented with general weakness, dizziness, lightheadedness 
thought to be secondary to new medication and hyperkalemia.  

# Weakness/dizziness: Historically occurs when she is 
hyperkalemic however this is also in the setting of starting 
baclofen for the first time in combination with dilaudid. No 
reported chest pain, however reported feeling mildly anxious and 
short of breath as well as racing heart. When seen in the ED, 
she had a K of 7.2 (hemolyzed) and 6.7 upon recheck 
(non-hemolyzed). She was treated with calcium gluconate in ED. 
Symptoms may be secondary to combined effect from baclofen 20mg 
(new medication for her) with dilaudid 4mg, in addition to K of 
6.7. Viral illness also of ddx, although pt without cough, 
fevers, abdominal pain, AMS. Patient treated with HD and she 
slowly improved. Dizziness is described as positional and she 
sees Dr. ___ (Neurology) for long term complaint of 
dizziness that comes and goes. It is thought to be from migraine 
headaches, although patient's dizziness in hospital was not 
always associated with headaches. Home meclizine PRN dizziness 
did seem to help. Patient evaluated by ___ and given persistent 
dizziness and her feeling unsafe with stairs at home, patient 
was referred to Rehab facility.  

# Hyperkalemia: Pt with history of ""many"" admissions for 
hyperkalemia. On arrival, patient had K 7.2 (although 
hemolyzed), but on recheck was 6.7 (non-hemolyzed). No 
concerning findings on EKG. Pt was given calcium gluconate in ED 
and then had several HD sessions. Discharge K 4.8.

# Right Heart Cath: Patient with history of pulmonary 
hypertension and is followed by Pulmonary clinic here at ___. 
Per Dr. ___ was to have admission for RHC in near 
future and given pt is already in house, she went for the RHC. 
RHC showed CI of 1.99 which improved with small bolus. Also PCW 
was 18 (had been 27 previously) which did not suggest pulmonary 
hypertension. Therefore, it was thought that acute on chronic 
DOE that patient had been complaining of for several months was 
likely from decreased intravascular volume in setting of 
aggressive fluid removal. Renal fellow discussed w/ patient and 
Dr. ___, agreed to higher dry 
weight goal of 44.5kg (2 Kg more than her previous dry weight).

# Left calf pain: Patient had tenderness to palpation on her 
left calf without evidence of swelling, warmth, erythema. Given 
patient's history of antiphospholipid syndrome and 
subtherapeutic INR (was lower than goal of 1.5-2), ultrasound 
was obtained. However ultrasound was negative for DVT.

# APS: INR on admission 1.4 (goal 1.5-2). Warfarin increased to 
3.5mg daily, however still INR 1.4 on admission.
